text.p: Australian weather forecasters said on Wednesday they had downgraded tropical cyclone Justin to a category one on a scale of five and had cancelled cyclone watch alerts along the Queensland coast.
"The cyclone, previously a weak category two is now a category one but gale force winds still persist out over the Coral Sea," weather forecaster Geoff Crane told Reuters.
The cyclone, the biggest to appear along Australia's east coast for 20 years, remained stationary with winds at its epicentre of up to 100 kph.
Australian Bureau of Metereology forecasters expected the cyclone, stretching over an area of about 1,000 km, to remain 650 km east of Cairns and 600 km east-north-east of Bowen for one or two days.
"It's such a big system, it won't disperse easily," Crane said.
